answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would.. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. Consider a ripple as the anchor of the cost.
